PC: Recommend comfort-focused care, which can include hospice, diuretics, inotropes, other cardiac meds, and opioids.
MK: Determine prognosis (or phase of illness) and medical options: o Home inotropes? VAD? Transplant? Hospice?
SBP: Make recommendations: o Specific advance care planning considerations at this phase: ▪ Health care proxy identification (which hopefully was addressed long ago) He is at risk of sudden death, so it is worth re-visiting limitation of LSTs, and making a recommendation with cardiologist’s input. Consider DNR recommendation, deactivation of ICD/CRT/VAD if applicable, avoiding re-admission to the hospital if applicable. Financial and emotional affairs: “In case things don’t go as we both hope, what things should you do now to prepare yourself and your family?’’
Mobilize community and family supports: palliative care, home care, hospice referral
ICS: Assess illness understanding: o Worth re-exploring, possibly reflecting back on prior conversations. If patient is unrealistic, may need to gently share that we’ve now moved into the final stages of illness (deepen awareness)
Revisit hopes, fears, goals and values: o “What is important to you now?” o “How do you want to spend the time you have left?”
